content.body:
Designed from the beginning to be a support tank, the Panzer IV benefited from some good early design decisions, allowing it to be upgraded constantly. In fact, it was the only tank that remained in production (one variant or another) from the beginning to the very end of the war.
Originally, the Panzer IV was meant for infantry support while its cousin the Panzer III series was meant to deal with enemy tanks. Thus the Panzer IV models A through D were equipped with a potent but inaccurate short-barrelled 75 mm gun designed to be employed not as an AT weapon but as an assault gun. Nothing could make a short barrel gun more accurate, but some efforts were made to increase the anti-tank lethality through the introduction of the 75 mm HEAT round. Relatively fast, it remained popular with troops and provided a sound chassis upon which future, better tanks would be built.
The Panzer IV is slightly larger than the Panzer III, but is essentially a good medium tank hampered by an inaccurate gun when engaging enemy tanks. Fine for point-blank blasting at structures (as it was designed to do), the dispersion on long range (600+ m shots) means ammunition can go very quickly just trying to establish a hit on difficult targets. The HEAT rounds are lethal and useful when you are able to get short-range shots on heavily-armored Allied tanks like the Char or Matilda.
The AP, HEAT, and HE rounds all have different ballistics, so you will need to practice to know roughly what performance to expect from various rounds (typically, HE/HEAT do not fly as far as AP). The range sights dial in for AP and this is the most plentiful type of ammo, so it is not a bad idea to range a target with AP, and then increase your elevation slightly before firing HE. Only at extremely short ranges, can you reliably expect to get any precision shots on enemy vehicles. Your armor is no better than the Panzer III, so at longer ranges you will find enemy AP rounds lethal and trading shots will not be a wise tactic on a regular basis.
The Panzer IV is reasonably fast, so it is a good tank to bring if armor’s needed in a hurry. In urban combat, its short gun is less of a problem, and can be quite a pleasure to use due to the short encounter ranges and the good lethality of the 75 mm round.
Your commander is only useful if he is able to see so leave him unbuttoned most of the time (pull him in during air attack or if you are entering an urban area). If he is killed, the slight risk to your tank through his open hatch) will have been more than offset by his utility to that point if you used him to spot for you.
Move quickly from cover to cover, scanning carefully. Use shadows and brush to break up your outline as much as possible.
CONTROLS & VARIATIONS:
Gunner (crew 3) has 3 ammunition types (AP, HE, and HEAT)
Gunner sight now has a fully-modeled multi-ammo sight; PzGr is the range for AP rounds, SprGr is the range setting for HE.
Driver (position 1) starts with the vision slit open. Press O to drop the shield. With the vision shield in place, the telescopic periscope works (press Numpad . to cycle through zoom levels).
As the Commander (position 2), press 0 to unbutton/button. Press Numpad . to cycle through binoculars.
As the Gunner (position 3) press Numpad . to cycle through zoom levels. Use Page Up and Page Down to adjust the range setting of the gun sights. Gunner can also open a vision port on the turret by pressing O and then Numpad 0 to see through it.
As the Hull Gunner (position 4) press Numpad . to cycle through zoom levels.
